```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(data.table)
a  <- file.path(params$root, "analysis")
S  <- readRDS(file.path(a, "did_sample.rds"))
unit <- S$unit
an   <- unit[T_ID %in% S$sets_r$SET]          # recipients in the analysis (recipient match)
fun  <- fread(file.path(a, "did_funnel.csv"))
cov  <- fread(file.path(a, "did_match_coverage_by_size.csv"))
bal  <- fread(file.path(a, "did_balance.csv"))
K <- S$settings$K
big <- function(x) format(round(x), big.mark = ",")
money <- function(x) ifelse(abs(x) >= 1e6, sprintf("$%.1fm", x / 1e6), sprintf("$%.0fk", x / 1e3))
kt <- function(x, ...) knitr::kable(x, format.args = list(big.mark = ","), ...)
```

This report describes how merger recipients are matched to comparison
organizations for the difference-in-differences analysis, and what the
matched sample looks like. Results are in the companion report
(`model-report.html`). Both are built from
`dev/analysis/did-recipients.R` and `dev/analysis/leadership-measures.R`.

# Treated units

**Mergers.** The treated units are recipients in two-party mergers
(`merger2`): one organization dissolves and transfers most of its assets
to one existing nonprofit, with evidence that the transfer was a merger
(leadership continuity on Schedule N or Part VII, or the filer's own merger
language). Schedule N filings run from 2010 to 2024.

**Time.** Time 0 is the recipient's tax year that contains the asset
distribution date. All years are on the recipient's own fiscal calendar;
the donor's years are on the donor's calendar.

**Observation window.** A recipient must file a 990 or 990-EZ in every year
from t-2 to t+2. The **baseline** is the mean of t-3 and t-2, with t-2
required. The baseline skips t-1 so that matching does not pick up a
dip or surge in the year just before the merger.

**One unit per recipient-year.** A recipient that received two donors in the
same year is one unit (17 cases). Recipients involved in another merger,
as donor or recipient, within the window are dropped, so each unit has one
clean event.

```{r funnel}
kt(fun[, list(Step = step, N = n)], caption = "Sample construction")
```

# Comparison pool

The pool is every organization-year `YEAR` in the full 990 panel
(`r big(S$pool_n)` organization-years, `r big(S$pool_orgs)` organizations)
that:

* filed in every year `YEAR-2` to `YEAR+2`, with a baseline in `YEAR-3` and `YEAR-2`;
* had no Schedule N involvement, as filer or named recipient, in `YEAR-3` to `YEAR+2`.

`YEAR` is the control's pseudo-merger year. Dollar amounts are in constant
2024 dollars (CPI-U).

# Matching rules

For each recipient, a candidate control must:

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Same NTEE group | first two characters (major group and first digit, e.g. `E2`) |
| Same calendar year | pseudo-merger year equals the recipient's merger year |
| Baseline assets | within a factor of 2 (log difference ≤ log 2) |
| Baseline expenses | within a factor of 2 |
| Baseline operating margin | within 0.10 |

Candidates passing every rule are ranked by a standardized distance: the
root mean square of the differences in log assets, log expenses, and
margin, each divided by its standard deviation in the pool. The **`r K`
nearest** become controls. A recipient with fewer candidates keeps all
it has. In the models each control is weighted 1/k within its set, so every
recipient counts once.

**Why the same calendar year?** Controls are allowed only from the
recipient's own year. The matched-set × event-time fixed effects then
absorb year shocks (the 2020 revenue shock, inflation) exactly. Allowing
other years would require separate calendar-year effects.

## Two matches

* **Recipient match.** Controls are matched on the recipient's own
  baseline. This is the natural comparison for "how did the recipient do?"
* **Combined match.** Controls are re-matched with the same rules on the
  combined baseline of recipient plus donor: summed assets and expenses,
  and a revenue-weighted margin. This is the natural comparison for "how
  did the merged organization do compared with the two separately?"
  It needs the donor's baseline, so it covers fewer recipients.

# Match coverage

```{r coverage}
cv <- cov[, list(`Recipient assets` = SIZE_BAND, Recipients = recipients,
                 `Matched (recipient)` = matched_recipient,
                 `Share matched` = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * matched_recipient / recipients),
                 `Median gap, log assets` = round(med_abs_logassets_gap_r, 3),
                 `Eligible (combined)` = eligible_combined, `Matched (combined)` = matched_combined,
                 `Median gap, combined` = round(med_abs_logassets_gap_c, 3))]
kt(cv, caption = "Coverage and closeness of the match by recipient size (baseline real assets)")
nctrl <- S$sets_r[TREAT == 0L, .N, by = SET]
```

The median absolute log-asset gap between a recipient and its controls is
about 0.13–0.15, roughly a 13–15% size difference. It is the same in
every size band. The largest recipients ($100m+) are matched almost as
often as small ones (87%). The unmatched ones are mostly the very largest
systems, which have no peer within a factor of two in the same NTEE group
and year. `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * mean(nctrl$N == K))` of recipients
have the full `r K` controls (median `r median(nctrl$N)`).

# Balance

Standardized mean differences (SMD) compare recipients with their
weighted controls, and with the whole pool in the same year and NTEE
groups. Dollar measures and employees are on the log(1 + x) scale. An SMD
under 0.1 is conventionally considered balanced.

```{r balance}
b <- bal[, list(Match = match, Variable = variable, Scale = scale,
                Treated = round(treated, 2), `Matched controls` = round(matched_controls, 2),
                `Pool (same year, NTEE2)` = round(pool_same_year_ntee2, 2),
                `SMD matched` = round(smd_matched, 3), `SMD pool` = round(smd_pool, 3))]
kt(b, caption = "Covariate balance at baseline (mean of t-3 and t-2)")
```

Matching removes almost all of the size difference between recipients and
other organizations. Before matching, recipients are about one standard
deviation larger than their sector peers. Equity ratio and months of cash
were not matched on, but they balance well too. Employees are slightly
less balanced (SMD `r round(bal[match == "combined match" & variable == "EMPLOYEES", smd_matched], 2)`
in the combined match), because the donor's 990-EZ filers report no
employee count.

# Sample traits

## Size

```{r size}
pq <- function(v) quantile(v, c(.25, .5, .75), na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE)
rows <- list(
  c("Recipient revenue", money(pq(an$R_REAL_REVENUE))), c("Recipient assets", money(pq(an$R_REAL_ASSETS))),
  c("Recipient employees (full 990)", round(pq(an$R_EMPLOYEES))),
  c("Donor revenue", money(pq(an[D_OK == TRUE, D_REAL_REVENUE]))), c("Donor assets", money(pq(an[D_OK == TRUE, D_REAL_ASSETS]))),
  c("Combined revenue", money(pq(an[D_OK == TRUE, R_REAL_REVENUE + D_REAL_REVENUE]))),
  c("Combined assets", money(pq(an[D_OK == TRUE, R_REAL_ASSETS + D_REAL_ASSETS]))),
  c("Transfer / recipient assets (t-2)", sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * pq(an$DOSE))))
st <- as.data.table(do.call(rbind, rows)); setnames(st, c("Measure", "p25", "Median", "p75"))
kt(st, caption = "Baseline size (mean of t-3 and t-2, 2024 dollars)")
```

The typical merger is a much larger organization absorbing a much smaller one. The median
transfer is a few percent of the recipient's assets.

### Donor size relative to recipient

```{r size-diagram, results = "asis"}
img <- file.path(a, "size_ratio_circles.png")
if (file.exists(img)) {
  cat(sprintf("![](%s){width=85%%}\n\n", img))
} else cat("*Run `dev/analysis/size-diagram.R` to draw this diagram.*\n\n")
```

Each row groups mergers by the donor's baseline assets as a share of the
recipient's. The recipient circle is fixed at 100%. The donor circle's
**area** is the group's median ratio. The groups are drawn at break points
that put 11–19% of mergers in each row.

```{r size-groups}
sg <- file.path(a, "size_ratio_groups.csv")
if (file.exists(sg)) {
  g <- fread(sg)[breaks == "suggested"]
  kt(g[, list(`Donor assets as % of recipient` = G, Mergers = N, Share = sprintf("%.0f%%", PCT),
              `Median ratio` = fifelse(MED_RATIO >= 1, sprintf("%.1fx", MED_RATIO), sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * MED_RATIO)),
              `Donor median assets` = money(D_MED), `Recipient median assets` = money(R_MED))],
     caption = "Donor size relative to recipient (mergers with a donor baseline; 2024 dollars)")
}
```

Donor size varies far less than recipient size. Median donors range from
about $0.1m to $1.6m across the groups, while median recipients range from
$71.5m down to $0.5m. So the ratio mostly reflects how large the recipient
is:

* At the top, small donors fold into large systems.
* At the bottom are near-equals, and mergers where the donor is larger
  than the recipient (14%, median 2×).

```{r dose}
kt(an[, .N, by = list(`Transfer size (FMV / recipient assets)` = DOSE_BIN)][order(`Transfer size (FMV / recipient assets)`)][
  , Share := sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * N / sum(N))], caption = "Transfer size")
```

## Year, sector, and affiliation

```{r year, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 3.2}
yy <- an[, .N, by = YEAR][order(YEAR)]
par(mar = c(4, 4, 1, 1))
barplot(yy$N, names.arg = yy$YEAR, col = "#1f5fa8", border = NA, las = 2, ylab = "Recipients", cex.names = 0.8)
```

```{r sector}
ntee_major <- c(A = "Arts", B = "Education", C = "Environment", D = "Animals", E = "Health", F = "Mental health",
                G = "Disease", H = "Medical research", I = "Crime & legal", J = "Employment", K = "Food & agriculture",
                L = "Housing", M = "Public safety", N = "Recreation & sports", O = "Youth development",
                P = "Human services", Q = "International", R = "Civil rights", S = "Community improvement",
                T = "Philanthropy", U = "Science", V = "Social science", W = "Public benefit", X = "Religion",
                Y = "Mutual benefit", Z = "Unknown")
sec <- an[, .N, by = list(L = substr(NTEE2, 1, 1))][, Sector := fifelse(is.na(ntee_major[L]), "Unknown", ntee_major[L])]
sec <- sec[, list(N = sum(N)), by = Sector][order(-N)][, Share := sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * N / sum(N))]
kt(sec, caption = "Recipients by NTEE major group")
kt(an[, .N, by = list(Affiliated = AFFILIATED)][, Share := sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * N / sum(N))],
   caption = "Affiliated donor-recipient pairs (Schedule R link, supporting organization, or shared group exemption)")
```

## Leadership and board outcomes

These are measured from Part VII rosters (`dev/analysis/leadership-measures.R`)
and are available for single-donor units with donor, recipient-before, and
recipient-after rosters.

**CEO.** The CEO is the person with a CEO, executive director, president &
CEO, administrator, or superintendent title. If there is none, it is the
highest-paid officer or key employee.

* The donor's CEO comes from its last roster at or before t0.
* The recipient's CEO comes from its last roster before t0.
* "Remains" means the person is on the recipient's roster at t+1 or t+2,
  in any role.

| CEO category | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `recipient_ceo_only` | Recipient's CEO remains; donor's CEO does not join |
| `both_ceos` | Both remain at the recipient |
| `donor_ceo_only` | Donor's CEO joins; recipient's CEO leaves |
| `neither` | Both gone |
| `shared_ceo` | The same person already led both, or the donor's CEO was on the recipient's roster before the merger |

**Board.** The governing roster counts trustees and officers, plus 990-EZ
listings. It excludes staff who are only key employees or highly
compensated, and former officers.

* *Retention* is the share of the recipient's t-1 roster still present at t+1.
* *Donor joiners* are donor members who appear at t+1 and were not already
  on the recipient's roster.

| Board category | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `intact_donor_dissolves` | Recipient keeps at least half its board; no donor members join |
| `combine_minor` | Recipient keeps at least half; donor joiners hold under 20% of seats |
| `combine_major` | Recipient keeps at least half; donor joiners hold 20% or more |
| `recipient_turnover` | Recipient keeps under half its board |

```{r lead}
lc <- an[, .N, by = list(CEO = fifelse(is.na(CEO_CAT), "(not identified)", as.character(CEO_CAT)))][order(-N)][
  , Share := sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * N / sum(N))]
lb <- an[, .N, by = list(Board = fifelse(is.na(BOARD_CAT), "(not observed)", as.character(BOARD_CAT)))][order(-N)][
  , Share := sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * N / sum(N))]
kt(lc, caption = "CEO outcomes among matched recipients")
kt(lb, caption = "Board outcomes among matched recipients")
kt(an[!is.na(CEO_CAT) & !is.na(BOARD_CAT), as.data.frame.matrix(table(CEO_CAT, BOARD_CAT))],
   caption = "CEO by board outcome")
```

A CEO can be identified for both organizations in
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * an[, mean(!is.na(CEO_CAT))])` of recipients. The
rest are mostly small, volunteer-run donors with no paid staff and no CEO
title. Board outcomes are observed for almost all of them. The most common
pattern is the recipient's board staying intact while the donor's board
dissolves. About a third of mergers bring donor board members onto the
recipient's board.

**Caution.** These categories are measured *after* the merger. They
describe how mergers unfold rather than being assigned beforehand, so
differences in outcomes across them are associations, not causal effects
of governance choices.
